metadata.title: Stališča osmošolcev v Sloveniji o vlogi vere pri vplivu na družbo: analiza podatkov ICCS

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses ICCS 2016 student questionnaire data from Slovenia (8th graders) and conducts secondary analyses. The authors state that they used the RALSA software, which accounts for the complex design and complex sampling of ICCS, implying that analyses were conducted in a way consistent with the survey’s sampling structure. However, the manuscript does not report specific weight variable names (e.g., TOTWGT/W_FSTUWT) or whether student weights were explicitly applied versus handled internally by RALSA. No plausible values are used because the outcomes are Likert-scale attitude scales and their correlations with other questionnaire items, so PV-specific weighting guidance is not applicable here.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The dependent variables are attitude scales and questionnaire-based items (e.g., attitudes toward the role of religion in influencing society, volunteering intentions/behavior, and European identity), not cognitive achievement scores for which ICCS would generate plausible values. Therefore, plausible values handling is not applicable to the reported analyses. The paper also does not describe any missing-data procedure for these questionnaire variables, so missing-data handling is treated as not reported.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Analyses focus on 8th graders in Slovenia from ICCS 2016. The authors report that ICCS 2016 included 135 schools and 2844 students in Slovenia, and they analyze only student data (teacher and principal data are not analyzed). The paper does not specify additional exclusions beyond the use of ICCS questionnaire scales and the computation of correlations; it also does not report any explicit missing-data rule (e.g., complete cases).

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ICCS 2016 the study leveraged the reported predictors to predict Primary study outcome (heuristic migration), finding that This paper reports secondary analyses of ICCS 2016 student questionnaire data focused on 8th graders in Slovenia (N = 2844). The authors construct an attitude scale on the role of religion in influencing society (S_RELINF) from six Likert items and examine its associations with (i) frequency of attending religious services outside the home, (ii) volunteering intentions and volunteering in community-help groups, (iii) expected electoral and active political participation, and (iv) European identity (E_EUIDENT from an “European module”). The reported results are correlation-based (Spearman and Pearson), showing a positive association between religious-service attendance and S_RELINF (ρ = 0.53, SE = 0.02, p < 0.001), weak but significant associations with volunteering (ρ = 0.11 and 0.14, both p < 0.001), and weak associations with future political participation (ρ = 0.12, p < 0.001; ρ = 0.05, p = 0.033). The study does not use ML prediction models, does not report any missing-data handling strategy, and—crucially—cannot support causal interpretations from correlations. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: This is not an empirical machine-learning prediction/classification study: the analyses are correlation-based using ICCS 2016 questionnaire scales (Spearman/Pearson) and do not train or evaluate ML models. Consequently, fields related to ML techniques and main_findings for predictive targets are intentionally empty rather than missing. The paper also does not provide details on missing-data handling, which is why missing_data_handling is set to not_reported.
